title: Reindexing, concurrent rebuilds and the lock each one takes

videos.script: An index is a copy. Some of the table's data, sorted, in files of its own. {{copy}} And a copy can stop matching what it copies. It fills with empty pages. A disk drops a write. Or the operating system is upgraded, and the rules for sorting text quietly change underneath it. {{drift}} Then the index gives wrong answers, and nothing in the log says so. {{wrong}} The cure is to build it again, and the danger is in how. A plain REINDEX locks the table while it works. You will open four terminals and watch a query that never touches the index wait for it anyway. {{four}} REINDEX CONCURRENTLY builds the new copy beside the old one, and nobody waits. But it waits for everybody else, and if it fails halfway it leaves a broken index behind, marked invalid. {{invalid}} You will make it fail on purpose, find what it left, and clean it up. {{clean}} And last, a way to ask an index whether it is still right. A check called amcheck, and an index built to fail it. {{title}}
